summary.text: A previously healthy 63-year-old female was found somnolent and confused at her residence after voluntary ingestion of metoprolol, digoxin, diazepam, acetaminophen/tramadol and chlorzoxazone in a suicide attempt, with a history of depression and declined psychiatric recommendations. On arrival she was bradycardic and hypotensive with a Glasgow coma scale of 12 and was moved to intensive care.

Work-up showed sinus rhythm with rare supraventricular ectopics and mild diffuse ST depressions, mildly raised lactate, and plasma positive for benzodiazepines and metoprolol with ethanol not detected. She received saline, a continuous epinephrine infusion for hypotension, gastric lavage and a lipid bolus and infusion, and was stabilized 4 h later.

On day 3, 12 h after epinephrine was interrupted, she developed intense retrosternal chest pain with ST segment elevation in V1 and V2, troponin I peaking at 10.8 ng/mL and a non-dilated left ventricle with LVEF 40%. Coronary angiography showed no notable epicardial lesions, and stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy was diagnosed.

Supportive treatment with fluids, aspirin, atorvastatin and a noradrenaline infusion led to hemodynamic improvement on day 6, when echocardiography showed complete LVEF recovery with normal wall motion, and she was discharged on day 8. At 3 months she was asymptomatic and attended psychiatric out-patient care for a depressive disorder.

ambiguities.description: Source conflict on the digoxin interpretation: the case text calls the plasma analysis positive for poisoning with digoxin (4.8 ng/mL), but the same paragraph says the plasma digoxin levels were low (so specific antibodies were not prescribed) and the discussion says the concentrations did not reach toxic levels. The 4.8 ng/mL value itself is undisputed; the flag and the digoxin poisoning diagnosis are review_only.
